text: Ụtụtụ ọma, nne m. Kedu ka ị boola?
english: Good morning, my mother. How did you wake?

text: Kedu ka ọ dị? Ọ dị mma, daalụ.
english: How is it? It is fine, thank you.

text: Aha m bụ Ugochukwu. Kedụ aha gị?
english: My name is Ugochukwu. What is your name?
My child is learning the Igbo language.
Come, let us go to the market.
We will eat in the afternoon.

text: A hụrụ m gị n'anya, nwa m.
Chukwu gozie gị na ezinụlọ gị.
english: God bless you and your family.

text: Ka chi foo. Ka anyị hụ echi.

english: It is raining today, be careful.

text: Ji na ofe onugbu dị ụtọ.
english: Yam and bitter-leaf soup are delicious.
Hello everyone! Welcome to our home.

text: Ege m ntị mgbe okenye na-ekwu okwu.
english: I listen when an elder is speaking.

text: Echi ka anyị ga-aga ahịa Eke.
english: Tomorrow we will go to Eke market.
He who brings kola nut brings life

text: Egbe bere, ugo bere; nke si ibe ya ebena nku kwaa ya
english: Let the kite perch, let the eagle perch; whichever says the other should not, let its wing break

text: Otu onye tuo izu, o gbue ochu
english: If one person plans alone, they fail
When a person agrees, their personal spirit agrees also

text: Aka nri kwọọ aka ekpe, aka ekpe kwọọ aka nri
english: The right hand washes the left, the left hand washes the right

text: Ọ bụ mfe ilu ogwe osisi, ma ọ dịghị mfe ilu ndụ
english: It is easy to cut a stick but not easy to live a life

text: Mmadụ bụ ihe kachasị mma n'uwa
english: A person is the most precious thing in the world
The king is in the mouth
Asking questions does not embarrass a person

text: Ndụ bụ ụzọ, ọ bụghị ọnọdụ
english: Life is a journey, not a destination
God blesses the hand in its labour

text: Osisi na-ada n'akụkụ ka ọ dara
english: A tree falls toward where it leans

text: Ụzọ bụ n'anya, ma ọ bụghị n'ụkwụ
english: The road is in the eye, not in the foot

text: Ụlọ dị mma mana o nweghị mmadụ
english: A house may be fine but without people it is nothing

text: Ihe di mma n'ọnụ adịghị mma n'afọ
english: What is sweet in the mouth may not be sweet in the stomach

text: Ihe mmadụ si n'obi ya pụta ka mma
english: What comes from the heart speaks better

text: Nke ọma abịa, nke ọjọọ gbaa ọsọ
english: Let good things come, let bad things run

text: Ihe mmadụ ji eme ihe bụ obi ya
english: What drives a person is their heart

text: Onye nwere obi ọma adịghị enyo obi ọjọọ
english: A person with a good heart does not wear a bad one

text: Ọ bụ ihe e ji n'aka nọrọ ya
english: What is in the hand stays in the hand

text: Chi onye adịghị ura n'oge ya na-aga ije
english: One's chi does not sleep while they are on a journey
He who brings wine brings peace

text: Nwata kọọ ihe okenye pụọ ọsọ, ọ dịghị mma
english: It is not good for a child to say what makes an elder flee
The right hand washes the left

text: Onye nwere isi agwaghị ya ka ọ dee n'ala
english: A person with a head is never told to use it as a pillow

text: Ihe ọjị eme na-eme n'oge ya
english: What kola nut does, it does in its own time

text: Ọ bụ n'afọ ya ka ọ na-eji ọrụ ya
english: It is from the belly that one pushes their work

text: Nwa mgbeke na-agụ ife n'oge mmiri ozuzo
english: The lazy child reads when the rain comes

text: Ihe onye metara ya adịghị egbu ya
english: What one has done to another does not kill the doer immediately

text: Nwoke bụ agụ, nwanyị bụ mmiri
english: The man is a leopard, the woman is water

text: Ọ bụrụ na ị maghị ebe mmiri bidoro maba gị, ị gaghị ama ebe ọ kwụsịrị
english: If you do not know where the rain began to beat you, you cannot know where it stopped
May the kite perch and may the eagle perch

text: A na-eji nwayọ eri ihe dị ọkụ
english: It is with patience that one eats a hot meal

text: Otu mkpịsị aka rụta mmanụ, ọ zụọ ọ zụrụ ndị ọzọ
english: When one finger touches oil, it spreads to the others

text: Ọ bụ mgbe ọ kụ na-akụ ka a na-akụ ya
english: The iron is struck while it is hot

text: Nwata bunie nna ya elu, akpụkpọ ya ọ mịnye ya
english: If a child lifts his father up, his own clothing covers the father's nakedness

text: Onye ji onye n'ala ji onwe ya
english: He who holds another down holds himself down too

text: Agwọ emeghị nke o ji bụrụ agwọ, umuaka achacha ya
english: A snake that fails to show it is a snake will be tied up by children as firewood

text: Ọ bụghị ụbọchị niile ka eji eri anụ
english: It is not every day one eats meat

text: Ebe onye dara ka chi ya kwaturu ya
english: Where a person falls is where their chi pushed them down

text: Mmiri riri enyi, ọ dịghị agba mmiri
english: The water that swallowed the elephant does not overflow with pride

text: Onye maara ihe ọ na-eme, ọ na-eme ya nwayọ
english: One who knows what they are doing does it gently

text: Nkịta si na ihe ya ji achị ọsọ bụ nʼihi na ọ maghị ihe na-eso ya
english: The dog runs because it does not know what pursues it

text: Ọ bụ nwayọọ nwayọọ ka e ji aracha ọka dị ọkụ
english: It is gently, gently that one licks hot corn

text: Onye lụọ ọgụ nna ya, ọ na-elu ya na mgbagbu
english: Whoever inherits their father's quarrel inherits its wounds

text: Maka na ọ dịghị mma, ka anyị jiri gaa nwayọ
english: Because the road is not good, let us go slowly

text: Ọ bụ ofu mkpụrụ ọka ka e ji mara ọka ọ chara acha
english: It is by a single grain that one tests whether the corn is ripe

text: Onye na-agba ọsọ na onye na-achụ ya nwere otu ebe ha na-eje
english: The one fleeing and the one pursuing are headed the same way
The feet that keep walking bring home wealth

text: Onye nwụrụ n'oge ọkọchị anaghị echefu ya n'udu mmiri
english: One who suffered in the dry season does not forget it in the rains

text: Nwaanyị mụta ọgụ mgba, ọ na-agba ya n'ụlọ di ya
english: When a woman learns to wrestle, she wrestles in her husband's house

text: Aka aja aja na-ebute ọnụ mmanụ mmanụ
english: Soil-covered hands bring an oil-filled mouth

text: Ọ bụ n'ọnụ ka mmadụ ji ama ezi okwu
english: It is by the mouth that one is known for truth

text: Onye buru ibu ọ ga-ata ahụhụ
english: He who carries a heavy load will feel its weight
Tell the story of Mbe na Nnụnụ (Tortoise and the Birds) freely in Igbo, 2-3 minutes, animated storytelling voice.
Tell any folktale you heard growing up, 2-3 minutes, in your own words.
Introduce yourself and your family in Igbo, 1-2 minutes, natural conversational tone.
Describe how to cook a favourite Igbo dish, 1-2 minutes.
Explain why the Igbo language matters to you, 1-2 minutes.
